title: Linear Graphs: Gradient, y-Intercept and y = mx + c
seo_title: Sec 1 Linear graphs and gradient Worksheets: Free Secondary 1 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
standard_text: Cartesian coordinates in two dimensions; linear functions y = ax + b; graphs of linear functions; the gradient of a linear graph as the ratio of the vertical change to the horizontal change (positive and negative gradients)
meta_desc: Free Secondary 1 linear graphs worksheets with grids: gradient and y-intercept, gradient from two points, equation of a line from its graph, parallel lines and real-life graphs. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: y = mx + c: m is the gradient and c is where the line crosses the y-axis.
key_sub: Gradient = change in y ÷ change in x. Parallel lines have the same gradient.
body_html:
How it works

Every straight line (except vertical ones) can be written as y = mx + c. m is the gradient (how far up for 1 across; negative means it slopes down). c is the y-intercept (where it crosses the y-axis).

Gradient from two points = change in y ÷ change in x. Parallel lines have the same gradient.

Example

Find the gradient and y-intercept of y = 2x + 1 (shown above).

m = 2, c = 1.

Answer: Gradient 2, crosses at (0, 1)

Example

Find the gradient through (1, 3) and (4, 12).

(12 − 3) ÷ (4 − 1) = 9 ÷ 3.

Answer: 3

Example

Find the line with gradient 3 through (2, 5).

5 = 3 × 2 + c, so c = −1.

Answer: y = 3x − 1

Common mistakes

  • Swapping m and c: in y = 2x + 5 the gradient is 2, not 5.
  • Using change in x ÷ change in y for the gradient.
  • Missing the minus sign when the line slopes down.
  • Reading the gradient of 2y = 6x + 4 as 6. Divide by 2 first: the gradient is 3.

faq.q: What do m and c mean in y = mx + c?
faq.a: m is the gradient (steepness) and c is the y-intercept, where the line crosses the y-axis.

faq.q: How do I find the gradient from two points?
faq.a: Divide the change in y by the change in x. From (1, 3) to (4, 12): 9 ÷ 3 = 3.

faq.q: What does a negative gradient look like?
faq.a: The line slopes down from left to right.

faq.q: How do I find the equation of a line through a point?
faq.a: Put the gradient and the point into y = mx + c and solve for c.

sets.title: Parallel lines and lines through a point

items.q: Find the equation of the line with gradient 5 that passes through (−2, 7).
items.e: Substitute the point into y = 5x + c: 7 = 5 × (−2) + c, so c = 17. y = 5x + 17.

items.q: Find the equation of the line with gradient −1 that passes through (3, −1).
items.e: Substitute the point into y = −x + c: −1 = −1 × 3 + c, so c = 2. y = −x + 2.

items.q: Find the equation of the line with gradient −2 that passes through (−2, 0).
items.e: Substitute the point into y = −2x + c: 0 = −2 × (−2) + c, so c = −4. y = −2x − 4.

items.q: Which line is parallel to y = 5x − 4?
items.e: Parallel lines have the same gradient (5): y = 5x + 5.

items.q: Find the equation of the line with gradient 3 that passes through (2, −3).
items.e: Substitute the point into y = 3x + c: −3 = 3 × 2 + c, so c = −9. y = 3x − 9.

items.q: Which line is parallel to y = 3x + 1?
items.e: Parallel lines have the same gradient (3): y = 3x − 5.

items.q: Find the equation of the line with gradient 4 that passes through (5, −1).
items.e: Substitute the point into y = 4x + c: −1 = 4 × 5 + c, so c = −21. y = 4x − 21.

items.q: Find the equation of the line with gradient −1 that passes through (−2, −6).
items.e: Substitute the point into y = −x + c: −6 = −1 × (−2) + c, so c = −8. y = −x − 8.

items.q: Which line is parallel to y = −3x + 7?
items.e: Parallel lines have the same gradient (−3): y = −3x − 4.

items.q: Which line is parallel to y = −2x + 6?
items.e: Parallel lines have the same gradient (−2): y = −2x + 1.

items.q: Find the equation of the line with gradient 5 that passes through (4, 6).
items.e: Substitute the point into y = 5x + c: 6 = 5 × 4 + c, so c = −14. y = 5x − 14.

items.e: Parallel lines have the same gradient (5): y = 5x + 5.

items.e: Parallel lines have the same gradient (3): y = 3x + 3.

items.q: Which line is parallel to y = 2x − 2?
items.e: Parallel lines have the same gradient (2): y = 2x − 4.

items.q: Find the equation of the line with gradient 5 that passes through (−2, −6).
items.e: Substitute the point into y = 5x + c: −6 = 5 × (−2) + c, so c = 4. y = 5x + 4.

items.q: Find the equation of the line with gradient −1 that passes through (3, 7).
items.e: Substitute the point into y = −x + c: 7 = −1 × 3 + c, so c = 10. y = −x + 10.

items.q: Which line is parallel to y = 2x − 5?
items.e: Parallel lines have the same gradient (2): y = 2x + 6.

items.q: Which line is parallel to y = −3x + 6?

items.q: A taxi fare is given by C = 2d + 3, where d is the distance in km. What does the 3 represent?
items.e: When d = 0, C = 3. It is the fixed charge you pay before travelling.

items.q: A taxi fare is given by C = 2d + 3, where d is the distance in km. What does the 2 represent?
items.e: The gradient is the rate of change: each extra km costs $2.

items.q: A candle is 20 cm tall and burns 2 cm every hour. Which equation gives its height h after t hours?
items.e: Start at 20 and go down 2 each hour: h = 20 − 2t, a negative gradient.

items.q: A plumber charges $40 call-out plus $25 per hour. Which equation gives the cost C for h hours?
items.e: $25 for each hour, plus $40 once: C = 25h + 40.

items.q: The line y = 3x − 6 crosses the x-axis at…
Which line is steepest?
items.e: Steepness depends on the size of the gradient, ignoring its sign. |−5| is the biggest: y = −5x + 1.

items.q: Which line slopes down from left to right?
items.e: A negative gradient slopes down: y = 7 − 2x has gradient −2.

items.q: Does the point (3, 11) lie on y = 4x − 1?
items.e: Substitute x = 3: 12 − 1 = 11, which matches. Yes.

items.q: A phone plan costs $15 a month plus 10p per minute. What is the gradient of the graph of cost ($) against minutes?
items.e: Each minute adds 10p = $0.10, so the gradient is 0.1.

items.q: S$1 = US$0.75. On a graph of US dollars against Singapore dollars, what is the gradient?
items.e: US dollars = 0.75 × Singapore dollars, a straight line through (0, 0) with gradient 0.75.

items.q: A line has gradient 2 and passes through (0, −4). What is its equation?
Which two lines are parallel?
items.e: Parallel lines have the same gradient: 3x in both.

items.q: Where do y = 2x + 1 and y = 7 meet?
items.e: 2x + 1 = 7, so x = 3. They meet at (3, 7).

items.q: A water tank holds 500 litres and drains at 25 litres per minute. After how many minutes is it empty?
What is the gradient of a horizontal line?
items.e: A horizontal line does not go up or down, so its gradient is 0.

items.q: The line through (1, 4) and (3, 10) has equation…
What is the gradient of the line?
items.e: From (0, −1) to (1, 1) the line goes up 2 for 1 across: gradient 2.

items.q: What is the gradient of the line?
items.e: It goes down 1 for every 2 across: gradient −12.

items.q: What is the equation of the line?
items.e: It crosses the y-axis at 1 and goes down 1 for each 1 across: y = −x + 1.

items.q: What is the equation of the line?
items.e: Every point has y = −2, so y = −2.
